subject: Reserved capacity SKU orchestration & performance-hedging question
thread_text:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Li <maya.li@signalpath.ai>, dev-ops@signalpath.ai
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity SKU orchestration & performance-hedging question

Hi Maya / SignalPath team —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Based on the workload details you shared (high-concurrency embedding generation + low-latency chat for support assistants) I sketched three reserved-capacity packaging options and a short rollout approach. See the draft offer attached and the SLA stub. High level:

- Option A — Memory-tilt (L40S-heavy): 12 x L40S (48GB) pool
  - Best for embedding throughput and large-batch export jobs
  - Perf/$: strongest on batching and memory-heavy jobs; weaker for single-request autoregressive latency
  - Price posture: lower per-hour GPU price, medium reserved discount

- Option B — Hybrid hedge: 6 x H100 (80GB) + 8 x L40S
  - Balanced: H100 for low-latency chat + L40S for batch embedding throughput
  - Perf/$: good across both modes if we route by workload; slightly higher overall unit cost than pure L40S but much better tail latency
  - Price posture: mid-tier commit with burst credits to absorb early spikes

- Option C — Performance-first (H100-dominant): 10 x H100 (80GB) pool
  - Best p95/p99 latency for chat and multimodal models; higher cost per GPU-hour
  - Perf/$: best for latency-sensitive inference but higher capex for you
  - Price posture: premium commit level with larger discount for 24-month term

Commit and discount structure (draft):
- 12-month commit: baseline discount 18% off list; 24-month commit: 28% off list.
- Add-on: 20% additional credit if you commit to H100-heavy pool and hit throughput bands in Q1.
- Canary: 2-week free canary (up to 5k queries/day) before provisioning.
- Throughput guarantee: we can guarantee sustained throughput per GPU (tokens/sec) and provide burst credits; hard SLOs for latency require H100 configuration (or hybrid with pinned H100 allocation).

Open questions for you:
1) Is embedding batch size and concurrency your priority over tail latency?
2) Do you prefer a single-pool deployment (simpler ops) or are you comfortable with a hybrid routing policy (we route by model/purpose)?
3) Procurement constraint: calendar vs fiscal year budget?

Attachments: SignalPath-draft-offer-20260711.xlsx (pricing table, perf curves), Redwood-SLA-draft-20260711.pdf

If you want, I can sketch a 12v24 pricing matrix (commit size x term) and one-line descriptions for procurement.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

From: Maya Li <maya.li@signalpath.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 10:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity SKU orchestration & performance-hedging question

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks, that framing is helpful. Quick clarifications from our side before we show to procurement: 

- Our embedding pipeline runs large batches overnight (batch size ~2048), so memory capacity matters a lot. L40S looks attractive there.
- Online chat/assistant traffic is spiky but small per-request; we care about p99 response time during ramp-ups.
- Budget: we have a constrained FY27 headroom; procurement prefers 12-month commitments but will consider 24 months for meaningful savings.

Can you confirm:
1) For Option B (hybrid), can you provide the expected tokens/sec and p99 latency numbers for both model classes (embedding model x1 and chat model x2)?
2) What does the burst credit model look like (how many credits, how long can they absorb a spike)?
3) Any constraints around KV cache hot-warm retention across H100 vs L40S? We rely on KV cache for prompt expansion and want predictable warm starts.

Also: procurement will ask for a single per-hour committed price and an effective perf/$ number we can use for internal comparisons. Can you convert the draft table into an "effective $ per 1M tokens" metric for each option?

If you can send a short pricing summary (one-pager) that maps to procurement terms, we can fast-track approval.

Thanks,
Maya Li
Head of Platform Engineering, SignalPath
maya.li@signalpath.ai

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Reserved capacity SKU orchestration & performance-hedging question

Karthik / Aditya — forwarding SignalPath's follow-up. They specifically asked for: tokens/sec / p99 numbers per configuration, burst credit mechanics, KV cache constraints, and an "effective $ per 1M tokens" metric for procurement.

My suggested playbook (thinking aloud):
- Offer hybrid Option B as primary. Reason: positions us as performance-aware while giving them batch economics.
- Pricing levers: 12-month -> 18% baseline; 24-month -> 28% baseline; we can offer an incremental 8% conditional rebate if they commit to H100-minimum share (>=50% of pool) and meet throughput bands (we measure via rollout telemetry).
- Burst credits: propose 72-hour burst buffer equivalent to 20% of committed throughput in month 1, stepping down to 10% in month 2.
- KV cache: commit to KV cache residency SLA on H100-backed instances only; L40S will have best-effort caching with warm-start guidance. We can offer sticky sessions for chat on H100 nodes for extra cost.
- Canary: 2-week free canary + 10k free token credit.

Concessions question: how far can we go on the baseline discount for 12 months without hurting margin? Also, do we want to include a one-time migration credit for their embedding pipeline?

Attachments: SignalPath-draft-offer-20260711.xlsx

Thanks,
Vanessa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Reserved capacity SKU orchestration & performance-hedging question

Vanessa —

Good notes. Quick math and constraints:

- Baseline perf estimates (rough):
  - Single H100 (80GB) for chat model x2: ~6500 tokens/sec sustained; p99 latency for short sequences ~120–180ms depending on seq length and model dim.
  - Single L40S (48GB) for embedding model x1 in batch: throughput ~18–22M tokens/hour for batch size 2048 (depends on model); p99 not meaningful for batched jobs.
  - Hybrid routing reduces tail for chat by ~30% vs L40S-only.

- Pricing lever sensitivity (back-of-envelope margin impact):
  - If list H100 hourly = $X (confidential internal list), 12-month at 18% keeps margin acceptable; pushing to 22–24% on 12-month will cut into runway unless we get a 24-month or a higher minimum commit size.
  - Adding a 8% conditional rebate (post-facto) is better than moving upfront discount — protects margin and aligns incentives.

- Burst credits: 72-hour buffer at 20% consumes capacity that we must provision; can model as refundable credits (apply against overage) rather than holding idle nodes. That reduces our ops risk.

- KV cache: agree to H100-backed residency SLA. For L40S we explicitly state eventual warm starts and provide guidance for pre-warming jobs (we can include an Ops-runbook in SLA appendix).

My ask: Vanessa, when you send the one-pager to SignalPath, include two clear procurement lines: (1) Effective $ per 1M tokens for their two primary workload mixes (embedding-heavy and chat-heavy), and (2) a simple table that maps commit size -> term -> effective hourly rate -> equivalent $/1M tokens.

If procurement pushes hard on 12-month discount, counter with (a) limited migration credit (one-time) instead of deeper up-front discount, and (b) conditional rebate tied to throughput metrics.

I can produce the effective $/1M tokens calc this afternoon if you want the numbers in the doc.

—Karthik
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
